attributes.action: Don’t Let School Leavers Get Left Behind
attributes.additional_details: Too many school leavers are struggling to secure their first job. Not everyone wants to or can afford university, yet many entry-level roles demand experience they have never had the chance to gain. Young people deserve opportunities based on their ambition, skills and potential. We want the Government and employers to work together to create more accessible routes into employment, apprenticeships and professional careers, including financial services. No young person should be left behind.
attributes.background: I ask the Government to work with employers to create more jobs and career pathways for school leavers, especially those who do not attend university, by promoting skills-based recruitment, apprenticeships and entry-level opportunities.

rejection.details:
Petitions need to call on the Government or Parliament to take a specific action. We can't publish petitions when the request is something that's already happening or something that has been announced since you started your petition.

We're not sure exactly what you'd like the Government or Parliament to do in addition to, or differently to, what it is already doing to support youth employment.

You could start a new petition explaining clearly what you would like the Government or Parliament to do to support school leavers.

In November 2024, the UK Government published the Get Britain Working White Paper which contained various initiatives to support more people into work. As part of the white paper, the government said it will establish a Youth Guarantee. This was in response to an increase in the number of young people who were not in education, employment or training (NEET).

Through this guarantee, the government will ensure that young people have access to further learning, help to get a job or an apprenticeship, and this support will be available across Great Britain.

On the 16 March 2026 the government announced further components to the Youth Guarantee, and referred to these as a “New Deal” for young people.

You can find out more about the Youth Guarantee in this House of Commons Library briefing: https://commonslibrary.parliament.uk/research-briefings/cbp-10827/

You may also be interested in measures the Government has announced to support apprenticeships: https://www.gov.uk/government/news/government-invests-in-young-people-with-more-opportunities-close-to-home

In November, the Government announced that its Jobs Guarantee scheme will be made available across all areas of England, Scotland and Wales. You can find out how the Jobs Guarantee works here: https://www.gov.uk/government/news/90000-young-people-furthest-from-work-to-be-given-guaranteed-job-no-matter-where-they-live
